summary: Regression-tested the purely structural refactor session (component/file splitting, no intended behavior change) across: Cyber Risk Scorecard full flow (index.jsx + useScorecardFlow hook + ScorecardNav/Footer + 4 split ScorecardResults sub-components), Blog post rendering (new pages/BlogPost folder with extracted markdown renderer/nav/footer/related-resources), AI page cluster (pages/AIPage folder split), Business Technology Assessment page (pages/BusinessTechAssessment folder split + embedded FreeAuditOffer tool), and backend POST /api/reports/email (split into 4 helper functions). Ran full backend pytest suite (54 tests) plus live browser end-to-end flows. Everything passed with zero regressions found - refactor preserved identical behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: CyberRiskScorecard/index.jsx cleanly delegates all state to useScorecardFlow hook and composes ScorecardHero/IndustryStep/Quiz/Results/Nav/Footer with no leftover inline logic - good separation of concerns.
ScorecardResults.jsx composition of ScorecardScoreDisplay/RisksAndRecs/FollowUp/EmailReport verified rendering with no visual/functional gaps between sub-components.

blogContentRenderer.jsx correctly handles heading+list-with-no-blank-line edge case (documented in its own comment) - verified bullet lists, numbered lists, bold text, and headings all render as real JSX, not raw markdown, on the SOC 2 blog post.

server.py email_report() split into _decode_and_validate_report_pdf / _get_smtp_credentials / _build_report_email_message / _send_smtp_message reads cleanly and preserves the exact same validation order and status codes (400 invalid PDF, 413 oversized, 422 EmailStr validation, 502 on SMTP failure) as before the refactor.

AIPage and BusinessTechAssessment folder splits (Nav/Hero/Framework/FAQ/CTA/AreasGrid/AnswerBoxes/RelatedLinks/Footer) all compose correctly with no missing pieces; invalid AI page slug correctly falls through to the NotFound page (404 UI).
test_credentials: None needed - all tested flows are public-facing

No DELETE /api/leads endpoint exists in the backend so these could not be programmatically cleaned up via API - main agent/infra owner should manually purge from the leads collection if needed (source_page values: cyber-risk-scorecard-followup and similar).
context_for_next_testing_agent: This pass fully covers the structural refactor described in the review request with zero regressions found: (1) Cyber Risk Scorecard - hero->industry(with insight note)->12-question quiz->results (score ring, risks/recs, ROI sliders) all verified; both Yes ('You're All Set!' + contact form submit) and No ('No problem! Feel free to email...') follow-up paths verified on fresh runs; 'Email me my full report' verified end-to-end with real SMTP delivery confirmation text 'Report sent! Check your inbox.'; Retake Assessment correctly resets to hero. (2) Blog post /resources/soc-2-compliance-guide-small-business - headings (5 h2s), bold text (8 strong tags), bullet lists render correctly (no raw markdown leaking), Related Resources + Related Articles carousel + nav All Articles link all work. (3) AI page /ai-readiness-assessment - headline, FAQ section render; invalid slug /ai-nonexistent-page-xyz correctly renders 404 Page Not Found. (4) Business Technology Assessment - '12 Areas', Technology Maturity table, answer boxes with links all render; embedded FreeAuditOffer industry-first flow (Construction industry -> insight note -> industry-specific job-site-connectivity question) verified working. (5) Backend: full 54-test pytest suite passes including the refactored /api/reports/email (valid send 200, non-PDF 400, invalid email 422, all still pass with identical behavior). Homepage smoke check clean, no console errors, trust/compliance badges and stats render. Minor pre-existing (not refactor-related) cosmetic note: AI page FAQ heading text is lowercase-slug-derived ('Common questions about ai readiness assessment') rather than title-cased - not a regression from this session, just an observation for a future pass if main agent wants to polish it.
